experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Observe the largest free-roaming elephant herds in Africa against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant families and exceptional photography opportunities, along with sightings of lions, cheetahs, and hundreds of bird species.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Track endangered black and white rhinos on foot or by vehicle at Ol Pejeta, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. The conservancy also shelters chimpanzees, lions, and wild dogs. A guided walking safari with armed rangers provides an intimate and thrilling wildlife experience.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Explore the alkaline shores of Lake Nakuru, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its breathtaking flocks of pink flamingos and over 400 bird species. The national park also shelters Rothschild giraffes, white rhinos, and leopards, making it a compact yet incredibly diverse wildlife destination.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Walk
experiences.description: Spend an evening with a traditional Maasai community bordering the Maasai Mara to learn about their ancient customs, warrior traditions, and deep connection with wildlife and nature. Includes a guided bush walk where Maasai guides share indigenous knowledge of medicinal plants, animal tracking, and survival skills.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange shared shuttle or budget matatu transfer toward Narok. The drive to Maasai Mara takes approximately 5-6 hours, so settle in and enjoy the changing landscapes as you head into the Rift Valley. Stop at a roadside viewpoint over the Great Rift Valley escarpment for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your boutique stay in Maasai Mara National Reserve. Check in, freshen up, and take a short walk around the camp perimeter to soak in the African bush atmosphere. Listen to the sounds of the savanna at dusk - distant hyena calls and birdsong are common.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during the flight
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or grab a quick affordable bite at a roadside kiosk near Narok town (ugali with sukuma wiki for around KES 150-200)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the camp or lodge communal dining area - opt for the set budget meal of the day, typically a hearty stew with rice or ugali (KES 400-600)

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared shuttle in advance from the airport to save costs - shared transfers can cost as little as KES 1,500-2,500 versus KES 8,000+ for a private taxi. Carry some Kenyan shillings in cash as ATMs are scarce near the reserve.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive inside Maasai Mara National Reserve starting at 06:00. July is peak Great Migration season - vast herds of wildebeest and zebra are crossing the Mara River from Tanzania. Head to the Mara River crossing points to witness one of nature's greatest spectacles. Look out for lion prides, cheetahs, and elephants in the golden morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp by 10:00 for a late breakfast, then rest during the hottest part of the day (12:00-15:00). In the mid-afternoon, join a guided bush walk with a Maasai guide around the camp's buffer zone - a budget-friendly way to learn about smaller wildlife, tracks, insects, and medicinal plants that game drives often overlook.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at a scenic kopje (rock outcrop) near camp - bring your own drinks from camp to keep costs low. Watch the sunset paint the savanna orange and gold. Return to camp for dinner and an optional campfire storytelling session with Maasai staff.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast - porridge, eggs, and toast included or available at low cost (KES 300-500 if not included)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch prepared by the camp to eat in the bush (request budget option, KES 300-400) or light meal at camp
meals.dinner: Camp communal dinner - nyama choma (grilled meat) or vegetable curry with chapati (KES 500-700)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your game drive through the camp or join a shared group drive to split the park entry fees and vehicle costs. Park fees are approximately USD 70 per person per day - budget for this in advance. Early morning drives offer the best wildlife activity and cooler temperatures around 18-22°C.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day game drive departing at 06:00 focusing on the Mara Triangle area, known for dense wildlife populations. Seek out the Big Five - lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino. July's dry conditions mean animals congregate around water sources, making sightings more predictable. Spend time observing a lion pride or cheetah family if located.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive through the afternoon, visiting the Talek River area. Watch hippos wallowing in the river and crocodiles basking on the banks. The afternoon light between 15:00-17:30 is excellent for photography. Keep an eye out for the endangered African wild dog if you're lucky.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp by 18:30. Visit a nearby Maasai village (manyatta) for a cultural experience - negotiate a group rate which can be around KES 500-800 per person and includes traditional dances, jumping ceremonies, and a tour of the village. This supports the local Maasai community directly.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast - hard-boiled eggs, fruit, and thermos coffee eaten in the vehicle or at a scenic spot in the reserve
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch in the Mara Triangle - sandwiches, fruit, and juice (budget KES 350-450)
meals.dinner: Maasai village may offer a simple traditional meal, or return to camp for a budget set dinner of beans, rice, and vegetable stew (KES 400-600)

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) for game drives - avoid bright colors that may disturb wildlife. Bring a light jacket as morning temperatures in July can drop to 14-16°C before warming up. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Morning game drive focusing on birdwatching - Maasai Mara has over 450 bird species. Hire a knowledgeable local birding guide for a few hours (KES 1,000-1,500) to spot secretary birds, lilac-breasted rollers, superb starlings, martial eagles, and the endangered grey crowned crane. The open grasslands and riverine forests offer diverse birding habitats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mara Conservancy or a community conservancy adjacent to the national reserve. Entry fees to community conservancies are often lower than the main park (around USD 30-50) and offer equally excellent wildlife viewing with fewer vehicles. Enjoy a self-guided nature walk within the conservancy buffer zone.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at camp. Attend a free stargazing session if offered by the camp - the Mara's dark skies away from city light pollution offer spectacular views of the Milky Way. July's clear skies make this particularly rewarding.

meals.breakfast: Full camp breakfast before the morning drive (porridge, eggs, fruit, tea - KES 300-500 if not included)
meals.lunch: Affordable local lunch at a simple eatery near the conservancy gate or packed lunch - githeri (maize and beans) or rice with vegetables (KES 200-300)
meals.dinner: Camp dinner - ask for the local Kenyan menu option which is typically cheaper than tourist menus. Ugali with beef stew and kachumbari salad (KES 400-600)

day_by_day.notes: Community conservancies are a fantastic budget-friendly alternative to the main reserve and your fees go directly to local communities. Ask your camp about which conservancies are nearby and most cost-effective to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Witness the Great Migration river crossing up close - position yourselves at a known crossing point along the Mara River by 06:30. Crossings are unpredictable but July is the peak month. Thousands of wildebeest plunge into the crocodile-filled river in a dramatic survival spectacle. Allow 3-4 hours of patient waiting for the best chance of witnessing a crossing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Oloololo Escarpment area on the western edge of the Mara for dramatic landscape views. The escarpment offers sweeping panoramas over the entire Mara ecosystem. Look for leopards in the acacia trees and large elephant herds moving through the area. This less-visited section often has fewer tourist vehicles.
day_by_day.evening: Photography golden hour drive from 17:00-18:30. The warm July evening light creates stunning silhouettes of acacia trees, wildlife, and the vast savanna. Return to camp and join other travelers for a shared campfire dinner - a great way to exchange wildlife sightings and travel tips.

meals.breakfast: Very early light breakfast at camp (fruit, bread, and coffee) before heading to the river crossing point
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at the Mara River bank - sandwiches and snacks packed by the camp (KES 300-400)
meals.dinner: Communal campfire dinner - budget BBQ with local sausages (merguez), roasted vegetables, and ugali (KES 500-700). Share cooking duties with fellow travelers to reduce costs.

day_by_day.notes: Patience is key at river crossings - herds can take hours to build up courage before crossing. Bring a good zoom lens or binoculars. Do not leave your vehicle during a crossing observation as predators are highly active in the area. The 25°C average high means comfortable viewing conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hell's Gate National Park (approximately 3-4 hours drive north toward Naivasha). This unique park allows self-guided cycling and walking - making it one of Kenya's most budget-friendly parks. Rent a bicycle at the gate for KES 500-600 and cycle through towering volcanic rock formations, spotting zebras, buffalos, and baboons at close range without a vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike through Hell's Gate Gorge - a narrow slot canyon with hot springs and geothermal steam vents. A local guide is recommended for the gorge descent (KES 500-800 per group). The gorge inspired the landscape of Disney's The Lion King. Swim in natural hot spring pools if water levels permit.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive toward Maasai Mara or overnight in Naivasha to break the journey. If staying near Naivasha, take an evening walk along Lake Naivasha's shores to spot hippos emerging from the water at dusk and hundreds of flamingos feeding in the shallows.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at camp before departure (KES 300-500)
meals.lunch: Budget lunch at a local restaurant outside Hell's Gate gate in Naivasha town - fish and chips or rice with stew (KES 250-400)
meals.dinner: Simple dinner at a local Naivasha eatery or back at camp - nyama choma with ugali and sukuma wiki (KES 400-600)

day_by_day.notes: Hell's Gate entry fee is approximately KES 1,050 for non-residents - significantly cheaper than Maasai Mara. The park is best visited midweek to avoid weekend crowds. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for the gorge hike. Carry plenty of water as the geothermal area can feel warmer than the 25°C ambient temperature.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Maasai Mara or explore Lake Nakuru National Park en route (slight detour). Lake Nakuru is famous for its flamingo populations and is home to both black and white rhinos - a rare opportunity to see all Big Five in one park. Entry fees are around USD 60 per person. Spend the morning doing a game drive around the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue game drive at Lake Nakuru focusing on the rhino sanctuary area. White rhinos are often seen grazing near the lake's southern shore. The park also has large troops of olive baboons and colonies of rock hyrax. Return toward Maasai Mara in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at your boutique stay in Maasai Mara by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at camp, reviewing your wildlife photos from the day and planning your final game drives. The camp may offer a cultural evening with Maasai warriors demonstrating traditional skills.

meals.breakfast: Roadside breakfast at a local cafe near Naivasha or Nakuru - mandazi (fried doughnuts) and chai tea (KES 100-150)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic inside Lake Nakuru National Park - request a budget box from your accommodation (KES 300-400) or buy from a kiosk near the gate
meals.dinner: Camp dinner back at Maasai Mara - welcome back meal of chicken curry, rice, and chapati (KES 500-700)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo population varies seasonally - July usually sees good numbers but call ahead to check conditions. The park is compact and easily covered in half a day, making it ideal as a stop-off point. Keep windows closed when driving through the baboon-heavy areas near the main gate.

day_by_day.morning: Final dedicated full game drive in Maasai Mara departing at 06:00. Focus on areas not yet explored - the Sekenani area or the Olare Motorogi Conservancy border. July's dry season means the short grass makes spotting cheetahs particularly easy. Look for cheetah mothers teaching cubs to hunt.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Maasai market near Talek or Sekenani gate if one is running (markets rotate days of the week). Browse handmade beaded jewelry, shukas (traditional blankets), and carved wooden souvenirs. Practice bargaining respectfully - prices are negotiable and buying directly from artisans ensures your money reaches the community.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography walk with a Maasai guide along the camp boundary. Learn to identify animal tracks, dung, and signs of nocturnal wildlife activity. As darkness falls, listen for the distinctive whoop of spotted hyenas and the roar of lions - sounds unique to the African wilderness.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast in the Mara - thermos of coffee, fruit, and boiled eggs eaten at a scenic viewpoint (KES 200-300 if self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Late lunch at camp after the morning drive - simple salad and sandwich or leftovers (KES 200-350)
meals.dinner: Special farewell-to-the-Mara dinner - splurge slightly on a grilled tilapia or chicken dish with traditional sides at the camp restaurant (KES 700-900)

day_by_day.notes: This is your last full day in the Mara so make the most of the early morning game drive. Ask your driver-guide to take you to any specific animals you have not yet seen. July's 30mm monthly rainfall means occasional brief afternoon showers are possible - carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning final game drive from 06:00-09:00 before checking out of your boutique stay. A quick 2-3 hour drive to catch any remaining sightings and say farewell to the Mara ecosystem. Pack up your belongings and check out by 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Maasai Mara toward Nairobi (approximately 5-6 hours by road). Stop at the Great Rift Valley viewpoint for a final panoramic photo. En route, visit a roadside Maasai craft cooperative to pick up last-minute authentic souvenirs at fair prices. Arrive in Nairobi by late afternoon and check into a budget guesthouse or hostel in the Westlands or Upper Hill area (KES 1,500-3,000 per night).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Nairobi's vibrant Westlands neighborhood on foot. Visit the nearby Karura Forest for a brief evening walk among indigenous trees - entry is KES 600 for non-residents and the forest is surprisingly wild given its urban setting. Return to your guesthouse and rest after the long transfer day.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast before checkout (KES 300-500 or included)
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop in Narok town - local restaurant serving pilau rice with beef and kachumbari (KES 200-350)
meals.dinner: Nairobi street food experience near your guesthouse - mutura (Kenyan sausage), roasted maize, and samosas from street vendors (KES 200-350) or a sit-down meal at a local restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Book your Nairobi guesthouse in advance - budget options fill quickly, especially in July which is peak tourist season. The shared matatu from Narok to Nairobi costs approximately KES 300-500 versus KES 8,000+ for a private transfer. Nairobi traffic can be heavy in the afternoon so factor in extra travel time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Nairobi National Park for a final wildlife experience - this is the world's only national park within a capital city. Entry is approximately USD 43 for non-residents. Spend 2-3 hours on a self-drive or shared game drive spotting lions, giraffes, zebras, and rhinos against the dramatic backdrop of Nairobi's skyline - a uniquely Kenyan photo opportunity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage near the park entrance - the visiting window is 11:00-12:00 daily and entry is KES 500. Watch baby elephants being fed and mudwallowing while learning about conservation efforts. Afterward, visit the Giraffe Centre nearby (entry KES 1,300) to hand-feed endangered Rothschild giraffes face to face.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Nairobi - head to the Carnivore Restaurant for a budget set menu or explore the Westlands food scene for affordable local dining. Visit the Maasai Market at the Yaya Centre or Village Market (check current days) for final souvenir shopping. Pack your bags and prepare for departure, reflecting on an incredible 10 days of Kenyan wildlife and nature.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or nearby local cafe - mandazi, chai, and eggs (KES 150-250)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Giraffe Centre or David Sheldrick Trust - packed sandwich or local cafe (KES 200-350)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range local Kenyan restaurant - try nyama choma platter with ugali, sukuma wiki, and kachumbari to end the trip on a truly Kenyan note (KES 600-900)

day_by_day.notes: Nairobi National Park is best visited early morning when animals are most active - aim to arrive at the gate by 07:00. The David Sheldrick elephant visit at 11:00 fits perfectly after the park drive. Keep some budget aside for airport transfers and any last-minute expenses. Nairobi's JKIA airport recommends arriving 3 hours before international departures.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs and collect luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Nairobi to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approx. 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by charter flight if budget allows). Settle into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around the lodge grounds with a naturalist guide to spot resident birds and plains game near the property.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome sundowner drinks on the lodge deck overlooking the savannah. Attend a brief safari briefing from your guide covering the week's game drive schedule, safety protocols, and what wildlife to expect during the Great Migration season.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at Nairobi airport — Wilson Airport café offers light sandwiches and coffee for around KES 800–1,200.
meals.lunch: Light snack box provided by the lodge upon arrival or a simple meal at the lodge dining area — included in most mid-range boutique packages.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the lodge restaurant featuring traditional Kenyan nyama choma (roasted meat), ugali, and sukuma wiki. Expect KES 2,500–3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Nairobi–Mara transfer in advance. Safarilink or Air Kenya offer scheduled flights from Wilson Airport for around USD 120–180 one way, which saves time. Road transfer via a private 4WD is more economical at USD 60–80 but takes longer. Pack a light jacket — evenings in the Mara can drop to 15°C.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning full-day game drive in Maasai Mara National Reserve departing at 06:00. Focus on the Mara Triangle and Musiara Marsh areas, prime zones for lion prides, cheetahs, and large elephant herds. Your guide will scan for the leading edge of the Great Migration wildebeest columns moving northward from the Serengeti.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive along the Mara River banks — the iconic crossing point where crocodiles ambush wildebeest. Pack a picnic lunch box from the lodge to eat at a designated scenic viewpoint. Look for hippo pods and Nile crocodiles resting on the riverbanks between crossings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge by 18:30 for hot showers. Enjoy a guided star-gazing session on the open deck with the lodge's resident naturalist, who will point out Southern Cross, Scorpius, and other constellations vivid in the clear Mara sky.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast at the lodge — a hearty spread of eggs, fresh fruit, toast, and Kenyan chai tea before the 06:00 departure. Included in lodge package.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch box from the lodge: sandwiches, fruit, juice, and a thermos of coffee eaten in the bush. Included in most mid-range packages.
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the lodge — typically a soup starter, grilled tilapia or beef stew main, and fresh mango sorbet. KES 2,800–3,500 per person if not on full-board.

day_by_day.notes: The Great Migration river crossings are unpredictable — your guide will monitor radio contact with other vehicles to position you at the best crossing points. Bring binoculars, a telephoto lens, and sunscreen. Wear neutral earth tones (khaki, olive, brown).

day_by_day.morning: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Walk — depart at 08:00 for a guided visit to a traditional Maasai boma (village) bordering the reserve. Learn about Maasai warrior traditions, livestock herding practices, and medicinal plants. Participate in a traditional jumping ceremony (adumu) and browse handcrafted beadwork jewelry made by village women.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided bush walk (2–3 hours) with an armed Maasai ranger along the reserve boundary. Track wildlife on foot — identify animal tracks, dung beetles, termite mounds, and smaller creatures often missed from a vehicle. Spot zebras, wildebeest, and Thomson's gazelles up close from a safe walking distance.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner game drive at 16:30 — the golden hour light is ideal for photography. Search for leopards in acacia trees and nocturnal species emerging at dusk such as servals, genets, and aardvarks. Return to lodge for a campfire dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast before departure — eggs to order, fresh papaya, yogurt, and Kenyan coffee.
meals.lunch: Traditional Maasai meal at the village — fermented milk (mursik) and roasted meat, or bring your own packed lunch from the lodge if dietary preferences differ. Village meal contribution: KES 500–800 per person.
meals.dinner: Campfire bush dinner at the lodge or a designated bush clearing — grilled meats, roasted vegetables, and fresh bread baked in a clay pot. KES 3,000–4,000 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai Village visit fee (approx. USD 20–30 per person) goes directly to the community. Bring small gifts like school supplies or ask your lodge what is most needed. Photography of community members requires permission and a small tip is appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — depart at 06:00 targeting the Serena and Governors' Camp areas of the Mara. July is peak migration season; millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles are moving through the reserve. Position along the Mara River for the best chance of witnessing a dramatic river crossing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue monitoring the river crossing hotspots. Crossings can last 30 minutes to several hours. Between crossings, explore the open grasslands for big cat activity — the Mara is home to one of Africa's highest concentrations of lions, leopards, and cheetahs. Look for hyena clans and vulture activity indicating a recent kill.
day_by_day.evening: Late afternoon return to lodge. Relax at the lodge pool or lounge with a Tusker beer or fresh passion fruit juice. Optional: attend a 30-minute presentation by the lodge naturalist on the ecology of the Great Migration and its conservation significance.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast at 05:30 before departure — scrambled eggs, bacon, toast, and tea/coffee.
meals.lunch: Full bush lunch at a scenic riverside picnic spot — the lodge prepares cold cuts, salads, fruit, and sparkling water. Included in lodge package.
meals.dinner: A la carte dinner at the lodge restaurant — try the Kenyan lamb curry with chapati or grilled Nile perch with coconut rice. KES 2,500–3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: River crossings are most likely in the morning between 07:00–11:00 and again late afternoon. Patience is key — guides sometimes wait 2–3 hours for a crossing to begin. Do not pressure your guide to move; the wait is part of the authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Maasai Mara at 07:00 for a road transfer to Lake Nakuru National Park (approx. 3.5–4 hours via Narok and the B3 highway). Arrive mid-morning and check into a mid-range lodge near the lake. Freshen up and head immediately to the lakeshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari — the alkaline lake shores host hundreds of thousands of lesser and greater flamingos creating a breathtaking pink carpet effect. Explore the lake circuit by vehicle spotting white rhinos (Lake Nakuru is a rhino sanctuary), Rothschild's giraffes, buffalos, and over 450 bird species including African fish eagles and pelicans.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drive along the Baboon Cliff viewpoint overlooking the entire lake basin — one of Kenya's most iconic panoramic views. The flamingo flocks glow pink in the fading light. Return to lodge for dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Mara lodge before departure — packed items to eat on the road if needed.
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop in Narok town at a local eatery — try pilau rice, beef stew, and a cold Fanta. Budget KES 600–900 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Lake Nakuru lodge restaurant — fresh tilapia from nearby Lake Naivasha, steamed vegetables, and ugali. KES 2,000–3,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru National Park entrance fee is USD 60 per person per day (non-residents). The park is fully fenced, making wildlife viewing very reliable. Flamingo numbers vary seasonally — July is generally excellent. Keep windows closed near the baboon troops at Baboon Cliff.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive inside Lake Nakuru National Park departing at 06:30. Focus on the southern sector for black and white rhino sightings near the acacia woodlands. The park also shelters endangered Rothschild's giraffes — one of the rarest giraffe subspecies. Look for leopards resting in yellow fever trees along the lake's eastern shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Lake Nakuru to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approx. 2.5 hours north via Nakuru–Nyahururu road). Check into a mid-range tented camp or lodge within or bordering Ol Pejeta. Afternoon at leisure — relax, swim, or take a short nature walk on the conservancy grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night game drive inside Ol Pejeta Conservancy (offered by most lodges, USD 40–60 per person). Spot nocturnal species including porcupines, spring hares, bush babies, and African wild cats. Ol Pejeta also has a resident lion pride active after dark.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the lodge eaten at a scenic stop en route, or a quick meal at a café in Nyahururu town — try mandazi (fried dough) and chai. KES 400–700.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ol Pejeta lodge — expect hearty safari fare: slow-cooked beef, roasted potatoes, and seasonal vegetables. KES 2,500–3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta Conservancy is the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos (Najin and Fatu). Entrance fee is USD 90 per person per day (non-residents). Book the northern white rhino visit in advance as it requires a special permit.

day_by_day.morning: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking — depart at 07:00 for a specialized rhino tracking experience on foot or by vehicle with an expert conservancy ranger. Track critically endangered black rhinos through the bushland using radio telemetry and traditional tracking skills. Learn about the northern white rhino conservation program and meet Najin and Fatu in their protected enclosure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Game drive through Ol Pejeta's open savannah — the conservancy hosts the Big Five plus chimpanzees at the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary (rescued orphans from Central Africa). Visit the sanctuary for a guided tour (included in conservancy fee). Also look for lions, elephants, and the large buffalo herds in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a scenic viewpoint with Mount Kenya's snow-capped peaks visible on the northern horizon (weather permitting). Return to lodge for a relaxed dinner and evening around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before the 07:00 rhino tracking departure.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the bush provided by the lodge, or return to the lodge for a light lunch of salads and grilled chicken. KES 1,500–2,000 if ordering à la carte.
meals.dinner: Special bush dinner at Ol Pejeta — many lodges offer a lantern-lit outdoor dinner experience. Three courses featuring Kenyan cuisine. KES 3,000–4,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino visit is emotionally powerful — Najin and Fatu are the last two individuals of their subspecies. Guides provide excellent conservation context. Photography is permitted. Tips for rangers (KES 500–1,000) are appreciated and support conservation work.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Ol Pejeta focusing on the Ewaso Nyiro River corridor — excellent for elephant herds, hippos, and crocodiles. The riverine forest also shelters olive baboons, vervet monkeys, and a wide variety of hornbills and kingfishers. Depart by 10:00 for the transfer south toward Amboseli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Long transfer from Ol Pejeta to Amboseli National Park (approx. 5–6 hours via Nairobi or the C58 southern route). Arrive at your Amboseli mid-range lodge or tented camp by late afternoon. Check in and take a short afternoon game drive within the park to shake off the road dust and catch the famous Kilimanjaro views.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at the lodge overlooking the Amboseli swamps — Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) often reveals itself at dusk when the daytime clouds clear, creating one of Africa's most spectacular backdrops. Elephant herds frequently cross the swamp at this hour.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Ol Pejeta lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the road or stop at a roadside restaurant in Nairobi's outskirts — try a Java House café for a reliable mid-range meal. KES 1,200–1,800.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Amboseli lodge — fresh lake fish, vegetable curry, and Kenyan chapati. KES 2,500–3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Amboseli transfer is long — consider breaking the journey with a brief Nairobi stop if needed. Alternatively, a charter flight from Nanyuki (near Ol Pejeta) to Amboseli takes about 1 hour and costs USD 150–220 per person, which is worth considering to save time and energy.

day_by_day.morning: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop — depart at 06:00 for a full-day game drive. Amboseli is home to some of Africa's largest and most studied elephant herds with tuskers carrying enormous ivory. The Amboseli Elephant Research Project (running since 1972) means elephants here are habituated to vehicles and can be observed at very close range. Focus on the Enkongo Narok and Longinye swamp areas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Amboseli's open plains — the park also hosts large lion prides, cheetahs, hyenas, and huge herds of zebras and wildebeest. The afternoon light on Kilimanjaro's glaciers is spectacular for photography. Visit the Observation Hill for a panoramic 360° view of the entire ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Guided cultural visit to a local Maasai community near Amboseli (different from the Mara visit — Amboseli Maasai have distinct traditions shaped by their proximity to Kilimanjaro). Learn about their cattle-centric lifestyle and coexistence with elephants. Return to lodge for a farewell Amboseli dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast at 05:30 — fruit, yogurt, and coffee before the 06:00 departure.
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch near the swamps — the lodge prepares cold cuts, salads, fresh fruit, and juice. Included in most packages.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at the Amboseli lodge — splurge slightly with a three-course meal featuring Kenyan-inspired dishes. Try the Amboseli lamb rack or grilled Nile perch. KES 3,500–5,000 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: July mornings in Amboseli are often crystal clear for Kilimanjaro views before clouds build by mid-morning. Position yourself with the mountain behind the elephants for iconic shots. The Amboseli elephant families have names (the AA family, CB family, etc.) — ask your guide about the individuals you encounter.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in Amboseli departing at 06:00 — a last chance to photograph elephants against Kilimanjaro in the golden morning light. Return to lodge by 09:00 for a leisurely final breakfast. Pack your bags and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Amboseli to Nairobi (approx. 4 hours by road via the C103 highway, or 45 minutes by charter flight). If time permits before your onward flight, visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage in Nairobi (open 11:00–12:00 daily, USD 7 entry) — a moving conservation experience with rescued baby elephants. Alternatively, browse the Kazuri Bead Factory or Utamaduni Craft Centre for authentic Kenyan souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations — head to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your onward flight. Enjoy a final Kenyan meal at the airport's Java House or Artcaffé restaurant while reflecting on an extraordinary 10-day safari journey.

meals.breakfast: Full farewell breakfast at the Amboseli lodge — eggs, fresh tropical fruit, toast, and Kenyan coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Nairobi café or restaurant — try Carnivore Restaurant near the airport for a iconic Kenyan experience (game meats and traditional dishes, KES 3,500–5,000) or a lighter option at Java House (KES 1,200–1,800).
meals.dinner: Airport dining at JKIA — Java House or Artcaffé offer reliable meals. Budget KES 1,500–2,500. Alternatively, grab snacks for the flight.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight departure time and allow at least 3 hours for JKIA check-in and security. The David Sheldrick Trust visit must be pre-booked online (free with advance registration, donations welcome). Kenyan shillings can be exchanged back to your home currency at the airport. Declare any wildlife products (legally purchased crafts) at customs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Observe the largest free-roaming elephant herds in Africa against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant families and exceptional photography opportunities, along with sightings of lions, cheetahs, and hundreds of bird species.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Track endangered black and white rhinos on foot or by vehicle at Ol Pejeta, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. The conservancy also shelters chimpanzees, lions, and wild dogs. A guided walking safari with armed rangers provides an intimate and thrilling wildlife experience.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Explore the alkaline shores of Lake Nakuru, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its breathtaking flocks of pink flamingos and over 400 bird species. The national park also shelters Rothschild giraffes, white rhinos, and leopards, making it a compact yet incredibly diverse wildlife destination.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Walk
experiences.description: Spend an evening with a traditional Maasai community bordering the Maasai Mara to learn about their ancient customs, warrior traditions, and deep connection with wildlife and nature. Includes a guided bush walk where Maasai guides share indigenous knowledge of medicinal plants, animal tracking, and survival skills.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, you will be met by a dedicated luxury concierge and transferred via private charter flight or premium 4x4 vehicle to your boutique lodge in the Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by charter).
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic transfer to the Maasai Mara. If travelling by charter, enjoy breathtaking aerial views of the Rift Valley and savannah plains. Arrive at the lodge, check in, and enjoy a welcome drink and orientation with your personal safari guide. Settle into your luxury suite and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the lodge's private viewing deck overlooking the Mara plains — a quintessential Kenya welcome. Followed by a candlelit bush dinner under the stars at the lodge's open-air boma, featuring a curated menu of East African cuisine with fine wines.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments and snacks provided during transfer by the concierge team
meals.dinner: Private boma dinner at the boutique lodge — grilled Maasai lamb, roasted root vegetables, and a selection of East African desserts paired with premium South African wines

day_by_day.notes: Pack a light jacket for the evening — temperatures can drop to around 15°C after sunset in the Mara. Confirm charter flight booking at least 48 hours in advance. Tipping envelopes for staff are provided at check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Early pre-dawn wake-up call with hot coffee and light pastries delivered to your suite. Embark on a premium full-day Great Migration Safari in a private, custom-fitted 4x4 Land Cruiser with a certified naturalist guide. Head to the Mara River crossing points to witness the dramatic spectacle of wildebeest and zebras crossing crocodile-infested waters — one of the greatest wildlife events on Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue tracking the Great Migration herds across the open savannah. Enjoy a gourmet bush picnic lunch served on fine linen under an acacia tree, prepared by your lodge's chef. Afternoon game drive focusing on predator activity — lions, cheetahs, and leopards are highly active during July.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a hot outdoor shower and relaxation. Pre-dinner drinks at the lodge bar with the day's wildlife photography review session hosted by your guide. Dinner at the lodge's signature restaurant featuring a five-course tasting menu inspired by local Kenyan ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast — freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit platter, Kenyan AA coffee and tea served in your suite
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush picnic — artisanal sandwiches, charcuterie board, fresh salads, chilled sparkling water and juices
meals.dinner: Five-course tasting menu at the lodge restaurant — pan-seared tilapia, Maasai beef tenderloin, passion fruit panna cotta, paired with curated wines

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Great Migration season — river crossings are most frequent in the morning. Bring binoculars, a zoom lens, and sunscreen. Your guide will radio-coordinate with other guides to locate the best crossing points in real time.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive hot air balloon safari at dawn over the Maasai Mara plains. Float silently above vast herds of wildebeest, zebra, and elephant as the sun rises over the savannah — a truly once-in-a-lifetime luxury experience. Flight duration approximately one hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-balloon Champagne bush breakfast in the wilderness, traditionally served on a white-linen table in the field. Return to the lodge and enjoy a midday spa treatment — choose from a signature Maasai-inspired massage or a rejuvenating body wrap using local botanicals. Afternoon at leisure by the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Walk experience. Spend the early evening with a traditional Maasai community bordering the Mara — participate in traditional singing and dancing, learn about bead-making, visit a manyatta homestead, and walk the bush at dusk with a Maasai elder guide. Return for a private dinner.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast in the field post-balloon — full English spread, smoked salmon, freshly squeezed juices, Moët & Chandon Champagne
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the lodge — grilled chicken salad, fresh fruit, iced hibiscus tea
meals.dinner: Private dinner in your suite or on your personal veranda — lobster bisque, grilled Nile perch, chocolate fondant with Kenyan vanilla ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon must be booked in advance through the lodge concierge. Weight limits apply (typically 100kg per person). The Maasai village visit includes a small community contribution fee which supports local education — your lodge will arrange this as part of the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Morning game drive focusing on the Mara Triangle — a less-visited, exclusive zone of the reserve offering exceptional wildlife density. Look for the Big Five: lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino. Your private guide will take you off the beaten track to hidden viewpoints and seasonal riverbeds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for lunch. Afternoon guided bush walk with an armed ranger and naturalist guide — explore the Mara on foot, learning to track wildlife, identify medicinal plants, read animal prints, and understand the ecosystem from ground level. This intimate experience offers a completely different perspective to the vehicle safari.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner stop at a scenic hilltop overlooking the Mara River with a private butler serving gin and tonics, local craft beers, and canapés. Watch the sunset paint the savannah gold before returning to the lodge. Dinner at the lodge's open-air fire pit — a social evening with other guests and live Maasai music performance.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge buffet breakfast — eggs station, tropical fruits, Kenyan honey, freshly baked breads, smoothies
meals.lunch: Lodge terrace lunch — grilled tilapia tacos, roasted vegetable flatbread, fresh mango sorbet
meals.dinner: Fire pit communal dinner — whole-roasted lamb, grilled corn, ugali, sukuma wiki, and a selection of Kenyan craft beers and wines

day_by_day.notes: Bush walks are subject to ranger availability and wildlife safety conditions. Closed-toe shoes and neutral-coloured clothing are essential. Insect repellent is strongly recommended for evening sundowners near the river.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer via charter flight or luxury road transfer to Amboseli National Park (approximately 1 hour by air). Check in to a premium tented camp or lodge with direct views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching experience — Amboseli is home to Africa's largest free-roaming elephant herds, and July offers exceptional sightings against the snow-capped backdrop of Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive in Amboseli focusing on the famous elephant families documented by researchers for decades. Your guide will introduce you to specific herds and their matriarchs by name. Also look for lions, cheetahs, hyenas, and hundreds of bird species around the swamps.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at a private viewpoint with Kilimanjaro glowing at dusk — a photographer's dream. Return to camp for a candlelit dinner featuring a fusion of Swahili coastal and Kenyan highland cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the Mara lodge before transfer — yoghurt, granola, fruit, coffee
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Amboseli camp — grilled vegetable wraps, cold cuts, tropical fruit platter
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at camp — Swahili-spiced prawn skewers, slow-cooked beef in coconut curry, rice pilau, and fresh pineapple dessert

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli's dusty terrain means morning and late afternoon light is best for photography — Kilimanjaro is most visible in the early morning before clouds build. A dust mask or buff is recommended during dry-season drives. Pack an extra camera battery.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day immersive elephant experience in Amboseli. Begin with a sunrise game drive to locate elephant herds at the swamp edges — the golden morning light against Kilimanjaro creates extraordinary photographic opportunities. Your guide will provide deep ecological insights into elephant behaviour, communication, and conservation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amboseli Elephant Research Project site (the longest-running elephant study in the world) for an exclusive guided briefing by a camp naturalist on ongoing conservation work. Afternoon game drive focusing on predator sightings and birdlife around Ol Tukai and Enkongo Narok swamps.
day_by_day.evening: Bush dinner under the stars with a private chef — tables set in the open wilderness with lanterns and a telescope for stargazing. The Amboseli skies are exceptionally clear in July, offering brilliant views of the Milky Way.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at camp — eggs your way, sausages, grilled tomatoes, Kenyan coffee and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the field — gourmet sandwiches, fruit, sparkling water served by your guide
meals.dinner: Private wilderness dinner — three-course meal with flame-grilled meats, roasted vegetables, and a decadent chocolate tart under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The Amboseli Elephant Research Project visit may require advance arrangement through your camp concierge. Stargazing dinner is weather-dependent — a backup indoor option is available. July is dry season in Amboseli, so dust levels can be high during afternoon drives.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning final game drive in Amboseli before transferring to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Laikipia (approximately 3–4 hours by road or 1.5 hours by charter). Ol Pejeta is East Africa's largest black rhino sanctuary and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Check in to a premium conservancy lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Ol Pejeta Rhino Tracking experience — an exclusive guided rhino tracking session on foot or by vehicle with a specialist ranger. Get close encounters with critically endangered black rhinos and the historic northern white rhinos (Najin and Fatu), the last of their species, under armed guard protection.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Ol Pejeta chimpanzee sanctuary at dusk — the only place in Kenya where chimpanzees are found. Return to the lodge for a premium dinner with fellow guests and a conservation talk by an Ol Pejeta ranger or scientist.

meals.breakfast: Final Amboseli camp breakfast — continental spread with local honey, fresh fruit, and Kenyan tea
meals.lunch: Lodge arrival lunch — light salads, grilled chicken, fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant dinner — slow-braised game stew, roasted sweet potato, Kenyan greens, and a passion fruit cheesecake paired with a fine Bordeaux

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino encounter is one of the most profound wildlife experiences on Earth — only two individuals remain. Photography is permitted but flash is prohibited. A conservation donation to the BioRescue Programme is encouraged and can be arranged through the lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at Ol Pejeta Conservancy — private game drive targeting lions, leopards, cheetahs, and large elephant herds. Ol Pejeta also has exceptional populations of zebra, buffalo, and giraffe. Your guide will take you to the Ewaso Nyiro River for predator and crocodile sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 2 hours by road). Check in to a luxury lodge overlooking the lake. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari — explore the alkaline shores of this UNESCO World Heritage Site, famous for its extraordinary flamingo flocks (hundreds of thousands in peak season) and over 450 bird species.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive around Lake Nakuru — the park also hosts white rhinos, lions, leopards, and Rothschild's giraffes (one of the rarest giraffe subspecies). Return to the lodge for a lakeside dinner with views of the illuminated flamingo shoreline.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Ol Pejeta lodge — eggs, bacon, grilled mushrooms, fresh fruit, Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box during transfer — artisanal wraps, fresh fruit, sparkling water
meals.dinner: Lakeside dinner at Nakuru lodge — pan-seared duck breast, wild mushroom risotto, lemon tart, paired with a crisp Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru flamingo numbers vary seasonally — July typically offers excellent sightings. The lake's alkaline water creates a distinctive pink shoreline. Binoculars are essential for birdwatching. Rothschild's giraffe sightings are near-guaranteed in the park's northern sector.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Lake Nakuru birding and wildlife safari. Begin at dawn at the lake's southern shore for the most spectacular flamingo and pelican photography in the soft morning light. Your specialist birding guide will help identify rare species including the African fish eagle, grey-crowned crane, and African spoonbill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Game drive through the forested areas of Lake Nakuru National Park in search of leopards (the park has one of Kenya's highest leopard densities) and the rare white rhino population. Visit the Baboon Cliff viewpoint for a panoramic view over the lake and the Great Rift Valley escarpment.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Nairobi via luxury road transfer (approximately 2.5 hours). Check in to a premium Nairobi hotel (Hemingways Nairobi, The Tribe Hotel, or similar). Farewell dinner at one of Nairobi's finest restaurants — a celebration of your extraordinary Kenyan journey.

meals.breakfast: Dawn breakfast at the lodge — full hot spread with fresh juices and Kenyan coffee before the early bird drive
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush lunch at Baboon Cliff viewpoint — charcuterie, cheese, fresh salads, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Carnivore Restaurant or Talisman Restaurant, Nairobi — signature Kenyan game meats, fine wines, and a decadent dessert selection

day_by_day.notes: Baboon Cliff is one of Kenya's most photographed viewpoints — visit in the late afternoon for the best light. The Nairobi hotel transfer should be pre-arranged through your concierge. Confirm your departure flight details and request an early check-in or late checkout as needed.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at your Nairobi hotel. Optional half-day experience: visit the Nairobi Giraffe Centre (feed endangered Rothschild's giraffes by hand) and the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust Elephant Orphanage (visit during the 11:00 public feeding hour — book VIP access through your concierge for an exclusive behind-the-scenes experience with the baby elephants).
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping at the Maasai Market or Village Market Nairobi — curated Kenyan crafts, beadwork, sculptures, and fine art as premium souvenirs. Return to the hotel for a final spa treatment or pool relaxation before departure transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in a premium vehicle. Enjoy access to the VIP/Business Class lounge for your departure flight. Depart Kenya with extraordinary memories of one of the world's greatest wildlife destinations.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet — full international and African spread, fresh smoothies, artisanal pastries, premium coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Giraffe Centre's on-site restaurant or a nearby upscale Nairobi café — avocado salad, grilled chicken, fresh juices
meals.dinner: Airport VIP lounge dining or an early dinner at the hotel — light Kenyan fare, club sandwiches, and a farewell Tusker beer or Kenyan gin cocktail

day_by_day.notes: The David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage VIP visit (private hour from 17:00) must be booked and paid in advance online — highly recommended and unforgettable. Allow at least 3 hours before your international departure for check-in and security at JKIA. Duty-free Kenyan coffee, tea, and local crafts make excellent final purchases at the airport.
